text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Italian coastguards said 1,500 Albanians refugees arrived in the ports of Brindisi and Otranto on Monday alone, and more were on their way, pushing the total who have made the crossing to escape to around 7,000 (all).
* Prime Minister Romano Prodi, on an official visit to Damascus, told reporters his country wanted to make sure the latest arrivals did not include criminals (all).

* Italian government called a confidence vote in the Chamber of Deputies (lower house) on a decree law to reform the milk sector. This relates to a package of reforms for the dairy sector which has been hit by a bitter dispute with farmers over strict European Union quotas (Il Sole 24 ore).
* Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini said he hopes the bi-cameral commission set to carry out constitutional reforms could settle "steady and lasting rules to cut public sector spending" (all).

* The lira fell to 1,003 against the mark following remarks by Germany's Finance Minister Theo Waigel who pointed out that convergence to the Maastricht Treaty criteria comes before the timetable for Eropean Monetary Union. Bank of Italy bought lira against marks at around 999 and but could not prevent the losses. The spread of the Italian 10-year Btp against the German Bund reached 215 basis points. Milan's stock exchange fell 2.19 percent (all).

* Bankitalia published a research report on the country's poverty, which showed it hit more heavily the young than the old and affects much more seriously the south than the north of the nation (all).

* After share ratio was set at 1.8 on Friday for Italian state telecoms holding Stet's merger with telecoms operator Telecom Italia, shares in Stet fell 4.12 percent and those in Telecom lost 5.05 percent (all).

* Hard-left Communist Refoundation party leader Fausto Bertinotti said said Maastricht Treaty criteria ought not to be considered and interpreted as dogmas, he also repeated his party is against cut in welfare and pensions (all).
* Post office workers went on strike and marched in Rome on Monday to protest against government plans to shut 4,000 post offices with the loss of about 10,000 jobs (all).

* Fedele Confalonieri, chairman of TV and advertising group Mediaset, said the group still aims to participate in the competition for the licence to operate Italy's third mobile telecoms network. The company's largest shareholder is Silvio Berlusconi, ex-prime minister and leader of centre-right opposition in parliament (Sole 24 Ore).
** Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
